transfer_provisions.section: Chapter IV, IV-3 (prescribed by the order)
transfer_provisions.quote: The officer in charge shall observe and shall require his subordinates to observe the regulations governing the occupation, preservation, and maintenance of Government-owned Foreign Service property prescribed by the Secretary of State, and shall be held liable for any damage thereto occasioned by waste, negligence, or improper usage.
transfer_provisions.note: Successor to EO 5624 (paras 2, 6, 7, 11-24): the occupation and maintenance of Foreign Service quarters is placed under regulations of the Secretary of State inside the same order that revokes EO 5624. IV-1/IV-2/IV-6/IV-7 (transfer of office, surveys, inventories) correspond to EO 5624 paras 3-5, 10 and 25; IV-4/IV-5 (recommendations and estimates) to para 8; IV-8 to leased quarters.

transfer_provisions.section: Chapter IV, IV-11 (prescribed by the order)
transfer_provisions.quote: Officers and employees of the Foreign Service may avail themselves of statutory leave subject to regulations prescribed by the Secretary of State governing the granting of such leave.
transfer_provisions.note: Successor provision for the subject of EO 5825 (leaves of absence); EO 5825 is not a target of any claim made in this batch (see the batch log).

cancellations_read: The 'Cancellation of Regulations' paragraph cancels Part I sections V-6, VI-1 to VI-3, VI-5 to VI-11, XVI-1, XVI-3 and XVII-1 to XVII-5 and Part II sections III-57, III-59 to III-68, III-70, VI-98, XXIV-429 to XXIV-433, XXIV-464 to XXIV-470 and XXIV-472 to XXIV-474 (OCR; numerals such as 'HI-57' and 'XXTV-429' read as III-57 and XXIV-429). It cancels Foreign Service Regulations provisions only; EO 5624 is a separate order, not part of the Regulations.
effective_date_reading: The revocation paragraph has no effective-date, delayed-effect or phase-in wording. The sentences 'This order shall become effective on July 1, 1939' that follow it in the held text belong to the next two orders printed on the page (EO 8190, Committee for Reciprocity Information; EO 8191, Goethals Memorial Commission), each introduced by its own 'Executive Order' heading and signature block. EO 8189 was signed July 5, 1939 (No. 8189), filed July 6 and printed 4 FR 2783-2785 on July 7, 1939. The project takes an order with no effective wording to be effective on signing, so the revocations are dated 1939-07-05.

targets_in_batch_07.EO:5624: 'Revocation of Executive Orders' list, item 2 ('Executive Order No. 5624 dated May 15, 1931'), 4 FR 2785; whole order, no qualifier
targets_in_batch_07.EO:5825: list item 4 ('Executive Order No. 5825 dated March 26, 1932'), 4 FR 2785; whole order, no qualifier (blocked at the earlier-end test, not at this reading)

conclusion: EO 8189 (signed 1939-07-05, 4 FR 2783-2785, read once in full from the held FR text) amends the Foreign Service Regulations by prescribing Chapter IV (Administration, IV-1 to IV-16), cancels listed Part I and Part II sections, and revokes five Executive Orders by number and date ('The following executive orders are hereby revoked': No. 5469, 5624, 5707, 5825 and 7013) with no qualifier, exception, savings or pending-matter wording. The machine ACT scope 'partial' and effective class 'unknown' for the EO 5624 and EO 5825 records come from a 3,900-character excerpt that spans the contents list and the three orders printed after EO 8189; the revocation itself is whole and carries no date. Chapter IV is the successor of the quarters regulations in EO 5624 (IV-3, IV-8) and the leave subject of EO 5825 (IV-11).
